manifest_semantics.expected_suppressed.matches: Expected Valgrind used_suppression context count; ranges or per-scenario exact values are enforced.
manifest_semantics.expected_suppressed.bytes: Expected suppressed bytes; null means Valgrind does not emit a byte count for that finding type.
manifest_semantics.expected_usage_lines_by_scenario: Optional exact count or reviewed bounded range of per-process used_suppression records for a rule in one report; catches an added or missing matching process even when each record remains individually in range.
manifest_semantics.required_usage: A required rule must be observed whenever this evidence set exercises at least one of its allowed scenarios. Rules whose real-product scenarios are not presently executable remain tracked but cannot be declared stale from an unrelated scenario.
manifest_semantics.usage_profiles: Optional exact, scenario-specific cross-rule tuples are enforced only where an exact lost-record partition is a valid behavioral oracle.
manifest_semantics.usage_profiles.evidence_identity: An exact-profile evidence identity names a locally reviewed, gitignored archive and its recorded checksums; it does not claim that a clean clone contains that archive.
manifest_semantics.protocol_ceilings: A protocol-derived ceiling binds variable Memcheck lost/reachable partitions to a fixed acknowledged lifecycle, pinned runtime/source identities, per-rule context/byte/block limits, cross-rule relations, and paired raw/suppressed evidence.

effective_inherited_sets.audit: Pinned wholesale because this is Ghostty's own regression suppression set. The current official base adds one reviewed Memcheck:Cond rule for Zig stdlib's documented unused DEFLATE Huffman entries (Ghostty c5f4f00ed); no Zentty-owned suppression was broadened. Duplicate rule names prevent name-only identity; hash, rule count, runtime usage, and the pinned Ghostty revision are therefore all checked.
Embedding-specific inherited rules cover loader metadata, Fontconfig, and GTK GIO initialization. The exact file is pinned and every used rule is retained in each report.
Valgrind built-in suppressions remain enabled in both raw and suppression-enabled candidate runs; raw means no Ghostty or Zentty suppression files, not --default-suppressions=no.

public_access.reason: The complete paired receipts are retained only in a gitignored local archive pending redaction, external attestation, and public artifact retention.

rules.affected: Ubuntu GLib 2.80.0-6ubuntu3.8 on amd64 when one process interns enough quarks to replace the initial 2,048-pointer array
rules.finding_type: Memcheck:Leak exact 16,384-byte definite allocation from g_quark_init constructor state
rules.justification: GLib 2.80.0 gquark.c deliberately retains the old quark pointer array so lock-free readers remain valid when the table grows. Upstream calls g_ignore_leak before replacing the pointer, but glib-private.h implements that marker for LeakSanitizer rather than Memcheck. The rule pins the exact GLib soname, direct constructor allocation, dynamic-loader frames, 16,384-byte size, and X11 scenarios; Wayland and unrelated GLib allocations remain unsuppressed. Interaction/X11 contains three real processes, but only the two or three processes that cross GLib's quark-table growth threshold retain this exact constructor allocation, so governance reviews a bounded two-to-three usage-line range while still rejecting disappearance or growth.
rules.reproducer: linux/tests/glib-quark-growth-memory-reproducer builds a Rust process that links GLib but not Ghostty, interns 2,500 unique quarks, and requires the exact 16,384-byte constructor finding. Source authority: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/glib/-/blob/2.80.0/glib/gquark.c#L284-300 and glib/glib-private.h#L98-117.

rules.rule_name: Mesa llvmpipe Ghostty instanced draw undefined values
rules.affected: Ubuntu Mesa libgallium 25.2.8 llvmpipe under Xvfb or nested Weston, Ghostty 1.3.2 instanced OpenGL draw
rules.finding_type: Memcheck:Cond undefined-value contexts in llvmpipe vector padding
rules.justification: The producer is Mesa's software Gallium driver and the required consumer is Ghostty's draw.drawArraysInstanced; the rule cannot match GTK-only or non-rendering findings. The 2026-08-21 interaction receipts reached the already reviewed global ceiling of 140 on both controlled Wayland and X11 while retaining that exact producer/consumer stack. The GH-97 full receipt also reached the same 140-context ceiling in single/Wayland with the identical pinned producer and consumer; the per-scenario ceilings admit that already bounded rendering variation without changing the rule or global ceiling.
rules.reproducer: Run linux/tests/memory-safety in a controlled software-rendered X11 or Wayland scenario; build/linux/memory-safety-Debug-interaction-{wayland,x11}.{raw,suppressed}.log preserve the reviewed 140-context observations. Upstream Mesa issue: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/issues/4880 documents Valgrind-visible undefined padding in Mesa code paths.

rules.affected: Ubuntu Fontconfig 2.15.0 and Pango 1.52.1 process-global metrics cache
rules.justification: The allocation begins in stripped Fontconfig and is consumed through the named Pango metrics API. Child rules are permitted only when this root is present in the same report. Public full runs 32121127845 and 32129794981 independently retained exactly two roots totaling 9,552 bytes. The 2026-08-21 receipts also retained one 4,405-byte interaction/X11 root and one 2,448-byte single/Wayland root. The later complete run retained additional roots with the same named consumer. The 2026-08-25 GH-93 rerun retained five single/X11 roots totaling 21,782 bytes and six interaction/X11 roots totaling 30,398 bytes in the affected processes. GH-97 receipts retained interaction/X11 roots from 1,709 bytes through six roots/30,398 bytes, interaction/Wayland observations through five roots/16,977 bytes, single/Wayland observations through five roots/14,841 bytes, and single/X11 observations from four roots/8,001 bytes through seven roots/25,387 bytes. The 2026-08-26 current-Ghostty receipts retained seven interaction/X11 roots/27,626 bytes, three interaction/Wayland roots/17,713 bytes, and six single/X11 roots/26,710 bytes; every raw stack retains the same Fontconfig allocation and named Pango consumer and every child remains root-gated. The suppression pattern itself was not changed.
rules.reproducer: linux/tests/ibus-focus-reproducer.c reproduces the root without linking Ghostty. Public run 32129794981 retained the paired raw and suppression-enabled receipts for the reviewed 9,552-byte observation; build/linux/memory-safety-Debug-{interaction-wayland,single-wayland,single-x11}.{raw,suppressed}.log preserve the reviewed 1,933-byte, 7,113-byte, and 9,601-byte complete-run observations.

Public runs 32121127845 and 32129794981 retained 30 contexts/960 bytes beside the same two metrics roots. The 2026-08-21 receipts include the reviewed 15/480 one-root floor plus later complete-run observations. The 2026-08-25 and GH-97 receipts retained 13/416 through 64/2,048 on single/Wayland, four/128 through 64/2,048 on interaction/Wayland, and 13/416 through 90/2,880 interaction/X11 children. GH-97 single/X11 receipts retained 90/2,880, 103/3,296, and 106/3,392 beside their separately reviewed roots. The 2026-08-26 current-Ghostty receipts retained 106/3,392 interaction/X11 children beside seven roots and a four/128 single/Wayland graph beside its separately reviewed root; each occurrence shares a process ID with a separately suppressed root and retains the exact narrowed stack. The suppression pattern itself was not changed.
rules.reproducer: The non-Ghostty Pango/IBus reproducer yields 30-32 matches/960-1024 bytes beside two metrics roots; build/linux/memory-safety-Debug-{interaction-x11,single-wayland,single-x11}.{raw,suppressed}.log preserve the complete-run observations beside their separately tracked roots.

rules.rule_name: GTK Pango Fontconfig metrics cache strings
rules.affected: Ubuntu Fontconfig 2.15.0 deep recursive string nodes owned by the Pango metrics cache
rules.justification: The prior one-frame Fontconfig rule was rejected. This rule requires strdup followed by five consecutive stripped Fontconfig frames and is valid only beside the metrics root. Public runs 32121127845 and 32129794981 retained 20 fragmented string contexts totaling 1,836 bytes beside exactly two metrics roots. The 2026-08-21 receipts preserve the same FcValueSave/FcDefaultSubstitute/Pango metrics ancestry, including 33/712 interaction/Wayland, one 116-byte interaction/X11 descendant, and four single/X11 contexts totaling 2,771 bytes. GH-97 retained one 45-byte/two-block interaction/Wayland graph beside three 8,810-byte metrics roots, 14/3,431 interaction/X11 beside its separately suppressed metrics root, and single/Wayland graphs through four contexts/4,056 bytes beside their separately suppressed metrics roots with the same narrowed ancestry. The 2026-08-26 current-Ghostty receipts retained 22/4,991 interaction/X11 and 13/5,251 interaction/Wayland string descendants beside separately reviewed metrics roots with the same narrowed ancestry. The reviewed ranges remain scenario-bounded with an unchanged root requirement; the suppression pattern itself was not changed.
rules.reproducer: With 40-frame receipts, the non-Ghostty Pango/IBus reproducer records the deep string descendants beside explicitly requested metrics roots. Public run 32129794981 preserves the 20-match/1,836-byte receipt; build/linux/memory-safety-Debug-{interaction-wayland,interaction-x11,single-x11}.{raw,suppressed}.log preserve the reviewed complete-run observations.

rules.affected: Ubuntu Fontconfig 2.15.0 and Pango 1.52.1 X11 layout cache
rules.justification: The consumer is the named Pango layout API and the rule does not match metrics-only or API-lifecycle scenarios. Local reviewed runs retained exactly two contexts with 20,865-26,208 bytes. Public full runs 32121127845 and 32143658025 on the same pinned Ubuntu Fontconfig 2.15.0/Pango 1.52.1 environment retained exactly two realloc roots and the exact Pango consumer stacks, totaling 13,285 and 13,253 bytes respectively. The 2026-08-21 receipts retained two roots totaling 4,418 bytes on interaction/X11 and 5,865 bytes on single/Wayland. Later complete-run single/Wayland processes retained up to three contexts totaling 181,371 bytes with the same named consumer and separately tracked children. GH-97 retained 1,677-byte roots in both interaction/Wayland and single/Wayland, single/X11 roots from 2,596 bytes through six contexts/385,036 bytes, and interaction/X11 roots from 1,723 through 3,736 bytes, each with the same named consumer and separately tracked narrowed children. The 2026-08-26 current-Ghostty qualification retained four interaction/X11 roots totaling 251,679 bytes; the unsuppressed receipt preserves the same realloc/FcFontRenderPrepare/pango_layout_get_size ancestry and the already root-gated child rules. The suppression pattern itself was not changed.
rules.reproducer: linux/tests/ibus-focus-reproducer.c calls pango_layout_get_size directly without Ghostty; the product interaction can also produce this cache. The public 7d7e3ca8 run retained raw receipt c6bbf33fc15f2a25dac12de47689d26e4588c09df672dc449176674deb012549 and suppressed receipt 9e8db97d04defbe3d790b99afa0412cbcfdd711dca617ea385e827b9337bad36 for the reviewed 13,285-byte observation; build/linux/memory-safety-Debug-{interaction-x11,single-wayland}.{raw,suppressed}.log preserve the complete-run observations, including the 164,200-byte process cache.

rules.affected: Ubuntu GTK 4.14.5 IBus module and libibus 1.5.29 in the controlled Xvfb/private-D-Bus/private-IBus xkb:us::eng environment
rules.finding_type: Memcheck:Leak definite/indirect IBusText preedit objects after focus-out
rules.justification: A standalone GtkIMMulticontext reproducer creates the same IBusText roots without loading or linking Ghostty. Four server-acknowledged focus-out/reset cycles with pinned GTK4 sync mode call the leaking external IBus clear-preedit path exactly eight times. The protocol ceiling permits only the source-derived lost-record maximum of 145 bytes and two object-rule blocks per call while retaining exact context and scenario limits; it does not eliminate Ghostty lifecycle responsibility.
rules.reproducer: linux/tests/ibus-focus-memory under linux/tests/controlled-ibus-x11; a required raw loss record contains ibus_text_new_from_string, libim-ibus.so, and drive_lifecycle in ibus-focus-reproducer.c.

rules.affected: Ubuntu GTK 4.14.5 IBus module/libibus 1.5.29 empty preedit strings
rules.finding_type: Memcheck:Leak indirect g_strdup child of IBusText
rules.justification: The full stack includes g_strdup, ibus_text_new_from_string, and the external GTK IBus module. It must co-occur with the IBusText root, its one-byte strings must equal its suppressed block count, and both stay at or below the acknowledged eight-call protocol ceiling. Independent raw and suppressed processes prevent one shared external service from coupling the receipts.
rules.reproducer: The standalone GTK/IBus raw receipt records the same one-byte strings without linking or loading Ghostty; linux/tests/ibus-focus-memory verifies the three stack anchors occur in one loss record.
